stories.text: The architect Albert Nelson Bromley designed these houses on Newcastle Drive in 1878, and died here in 1934. His buildings in the city include Boots' stores on Pelham Street and Turney Street. stories.text: Jessie Batten, a London graduate of 1892, owned Western House school here from 1895. She married in 1910 but kept her own name at work, and retired in 1918.

Louisa Clarke opened a day and boarding school for girls in 1874, at 9 Park Terrace; called Western House, it moved here, to 30 The Ropewalk, in 1890. Rose Feilmann, who wrote "There are fairies at the bottom of my garden", was one of her pupils.

stories.text: The Playhouse began in 1948 as a repertory theatre in a former cinema on Goldsmith Street. Its present building, a modernist theatre designed by Peter Moro, opened here in 1963. In 2001 Anish Kapoor's Sky Mirror was put up between the theatre and Wellington Circus, and in 2004 the building was restored with a Heritage Lottery Fund grant.
The architect Peter Moro designed the Playhouse.[^s1][^s2]
